questions.question: 1. Which of the following sorting algorithms, in its typical implementation, gives the best performance when applied to an array that is sorted or almost sorted (with at most 1 or 2 elements misplaced)?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Quick Sort does not specifically exploit the fact that only a small number of elements are misplaced, and its performance depends on the partitioning strategy.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Heap Sort does not generally take advantage of an already sorted or nearly sorted input.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Standard Merge Sort does not generally reduce its work substantially just because the input is nearly sorted.
explanations.d: Correct. Insertion Sort can take advantage of near-sorted order and can run in $O(n)$ time when the input is already sorted.

questions.question: 2. Consider a full binary min-heap containing $n$ elements with distinct keys. What is the probability that the largest element is at the last level?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This value does not follow from the structural and ordering properties stated in the question.
explanations.b: Correct. In a min-heap with distinct keys, the largest element must be a leaf. In a full binary heap, all leaves are at the last level, so the probability is 1.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The largest element is not restricted to one predetermined node among the $n$ nodes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This expression does not represent the placement property imposed by the min-heap structure.

questions.question: 3. In a max-heap, the element with the greatest key is always in which node?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A leaf is not required to contain the greatest key in a max-heap.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The first node of the left subtree is not guaranteed to contain the greatest key.
explanations.c: Correct. By the max-heap property, the root contains the greatest key.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The first node of the right subtree is not guaranteed to contain the greatest key.

questions.question: 4. Heap can also be used as _______.

explanations.a: Correct. A heap is commonly used to implement a priority queue, where the highest- or lowest-priority element can be accessed efficiently.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A stack follows the LIFO principle, which is different from the ordering maintained by a heap.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A heap satisfies a parent-child ordering property but does not keep the entire array in decreasing order.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The data structure has a standard application that matches the priority-queue model.

questions.question: 5. An array consists of $n$ elements. We want to create a heap using these elements. The time complexity of building a heap will be in the order of ________.

explanations.a: Incorrect. This bound is much larger than the time required by the bottom-up heap construction method.
explanations.b: Correct. A heap can be built from an array of $n$ elements in $O(n)$ time using bottom-up construction.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Bottom-up heap construction does not require quadratic time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This expression is not the standard time complexity for bottom-up heap construction.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following is the main reason Heap Sort has $O(n\log n)$ worst-case time complexity?

answers.a: It performs a linear search for every element
answers.b: It repeatedly partitions the array into equal halves
answers.c: It compares every pair of elements
answers.d: It performs a linear number of heap adjustments, each taking up to $O(\log n)$ time

explanations.a: Incorrect. Heap Sort does not perform a full linear search for every extracted element.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Heap Sort does not use recursive equal-halving partitioning as its main operation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Comparing every pair of elements would lead to a quadratic number of comparisons.
explanations.d: Correct. Heap construction is linear with the bottom-up method, and repeated extraction with heap restoration contributes $O(n\log n)$ in the worst case.

questions.question: 7. Which of the following statements about Heap Sort is correct?

answers.b: Heap Sort can be implemented in-place with $O(1)$ auxiliary space
answers.c: Heap Sort requires a second array of size $n$
answers.d: Heap Sort is stable in its standard in-place implementation

explanations.a: Incorrect. Heap Sort has a tighter worst-case bound than quadratic time.
explanations.b: Correct. Heap Sort can be performed in-place using constant auxiliary space, apart from the input array.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A standard in-place implementation does not require a second array of size $n$.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Standard Heap Sort is generally not stable because equal-key elements can change their relative order.

questions.question: 8. For ascending-order Heap Sort, why is a max-heap commonly used?

answers.a: Because the maximum element can be placed at the end of the unsorted portion after each extraction
answers.b: Because a max-heap automatically sorts the array without extraction
answers.c: Because a max-heap always contains the minimum element at the root
answers.d: Because max-heaps require no comparisons during sorting

explanations.a: Correct. The maximum element is available at the root and can be moved to the end of the active unsorted portion, building the sorted suffix.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Constructing the heap alone does not finish the sorting process.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This statement describes the root property of a min-heap, not a max-heap.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Heap construction and restoration depend on comparisons between keys.

questions.question: 9. If the input array contains $n$ elements, what is the worst-case time complexity of Heap Sort?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Heap Sort performs repeated heap adjustments in addition to processing the elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A logarithmic bound applies to the height of the heap or an individual heap adjustment, not the complete sorting process.
explanations.c: Correct. Heap Sort has $O(n\log n)$ worst-case time complexity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The heap structure prevents the worst-case sorting time from becoming quadratic.
